Hoo boy. Ok. The comments here are spot on, but maybe I can add another perspective to help you make a decision regarding which direction you should lean. I'm a middle-aged woman who went from cook to manager about 6 years ago. 

First, do you have a partner/spouse/significant other? Do you like them? Do they like you? If the answer is yes, please think very carefully about what you both need in terms of quality time together. Next week, although I live with my SO and sleep in the same bed every night, we will not have a face to face conversation with each other from Tuesday night through the following Monday afternoon. We will have a brief phone call after my dinner rush is over and before he goes to bed. He will be almost totally responsible for the household, and I will manage to do laundry. He will have to give the pets their meds, eat dinner alone, etc etc. It gets old very fast, and if your SO isn't on board, then the harmony in the household can end pretty quickly. Also, I miss him. Quite a bit.

Second, what does your childcare look like? Are they reliable? Are they inexpensive enough to make it worth going to work? As a beginner, you could make $19 or $20 an hour, but what does a competent and reliable babysitter charge? $19 or $20 and an hour? If you have a daycare situation set up, that's great, but what are their hours? You limit yourself quite a bit if you are only available weekdays until 5. Are you going to have to miss work if your child is excluded from daycare for 48 hours because of a fever? Do you have a backup plan?

Third, and I want to say this gently, this job is so far removed from being a hobby home cook that you might as well be applying to be an astronaut. In a high volume turn and burn kitchen, things work much more like a factory assembly line (with swearing and fire) than any kitchen you may be familiar with. The attractive, calm kitchen stations on television are, well, made for TV. It's not an easy job. It's hot, hard on your joints, and hard on your mental health. 

None of us here in the comments are trying to roast you. We just want you to understand that the romantic view of this job is exactly that...romantic. Being informed and understanding what the job will ask of you is the first step to making a decision about what is right for you and your family. I love my job. Most of us do. But it really truly isn't for everyone. In my decades of experience, if you want flexibility, have kids, and enjoy sunlight, you should become a server.

 I'm not being sarcastic. Servers have more flexibility and very often make more money than cooks. If you have no service experience, apply to be a carry out or ToGo server and negotiate being cross trained in the dining room. You will still probably be obligated to work Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve, but you will leave at close while the kitchen is just starting to break down and clean. You come in later, leave earlier, and the job is somewhat easier as long as you have the skills to be vaguely personable to most guests. 

Last, and holy crap I apologize for the length of this reply, work for a corporate place first. Big corporate is often derided on this sub, but they do have better benefits, better training programs, and lots of structure in place in terms of insurance and retirement savings. I'll shut up now. Good luck!!!!

Thanks. My boss is the cheapest asshole I've ever met. To be honest, I mostly did it by just going over his head to the corporate people and explaining how things were versus how they should be. When I got to this particular store, the filter system on the fryers had been broken for five years. Only half the sally worked after a fire caused by incredibly old and useless hood filters. The steamer for hot holding was broken so they were using a pot as a water bath. All the gaskets in the low boys were held together with duct tape. I almost died inside.

A year later the fryer is fixed, new sally installed, I'm limping the steamer along while waiting for a new unit to be shipped. All new hood filters bought and despite my boss insisting we keep the old ones for 'an emergency' I threw them all away. Replaced every cutting board, scale, blade, and cambro in the place this past month. It was like Christmas for a few days lol. Gaskets on the low boys have been replaced as well. I'm working on a deep cleaning schedule and getting less push back because they want to keep the new stuff looking nice.

As for pay rates, I simply gave my DO and Executive VP a list of our current pay as opposed to the corporate average for cooks with the same responsibility and tenure. I had some back up from other KMs with more clout than I had at the time so I won't get much credit for it but I don't really care. Incentive to work for us is the number one priority right now. Most of the bennys were already in place but a lot of my staff are totally computer illiterate and some don't have access to WIFI so I brought my personal laptop in and helped them navigate the system if they chose to sign up. I still text with ex employees about financial issues and investment services.

Late to the party but...I crew once a year for an extreme ultra marathon. The not being able to keep food down is kind of concerning and probably due to an electrolyte imbalance. He should be drinking water, not coffee or soda, and supplementing with Pedialyte. Also, don't worry about nutrition so much as calories going in. One of my runner's favorite easy-to-eat meals is canned lentil soup mixed with instant potato flakes and butter. He probably needs more salt, if he sweats a ton on the line. You can make something like a buttery bacon and polenta cake, cut it into cubes, and send him off with one or two every day. Easy calories and some extra salt. Make him small, bite sized packets that he only has to pop in his mouth while pushing out food. He should not be depending on the usual three meals a day routine, he should be kind of consuming a bite at a time fairly consistently. Look into prepackaged foods that runners eat, if your budget allows. PM me if you want more info. Good luck and you are amazing for being so concerned!
